submitted.rationale: Of the three measurements, the Co-rich composition (Ca0.14 Co0.70 Mn0.16) had the highest photocurrent, at 3e-8 A. MACE puts the Co3O4 spinel on the convex hull.

rejected.reason: Mn-rich corner measured 0 A. MEGNet gives the Mn-oxide reference a near-zero PBE gap.
Ca-rich region measured -5e-8 A (cathodic, so no photoanode activity).

consultations.verdict: Weakly supportive: MEGNet gives ~0 eV gap for mp-18748 (Co-rich spinel, metallic-like, poor photoanode) and ~0.94 eV for mp-18759 (Mn-oxide), suggesting Mn-rich regions have a finite gap and may give photocurrent under 3.2 eV light. Uninformative about ternary mixing; measuring Mn-rich corner first as exploration.

Supportive for exploration: MACE puts Co3O4 spinel on the hull, so Co-rich films likely crystallize as stable spinel (absorbs strongly at 3.2 eV). Mn-rich corner gave zero, so test the opposite (Co-rich) region.

Uninformative/weakly against Mn-rich: PBE gap of the Mn-oxide reference is ~0, consistent with the zero photocurrent at the Mn corner. The Ca-rich/Co-moderate region is unexplored and could host Ca-containing mixed oxides; since max-merit scoring rewards exploration and Co-rich already secured 3e-8, measure Ca-rich index 10.
